content.thinking:
Hmm! The fib_max build produced 400000 rows, not 400001. Let me think: 200000 /64 prefixes at keys 0, 2, 4, ..., 399998. Boundaries: 0, starts {0,2,4,...,399998}, ends {1,3,5,...,399999}. So bounds = {0,1,2,3,...,399999} = 400000 distinct values. So rows = 400000, not 400001. My earlier estimate of 400001 assumed all starts and ends are distinct from each other and from 0 — here they interleave so the union is 400000. Fine, that's correct behavior (the bound is 400001, and this case yields 400000).

To actually hit 400001 rows, I'd need 200000 prefixes whose starts and ends are all distinct and none is 0... e.g., /64 prefixes at odd keys 1,3,5,...? Then starts = {1,3,...}, ends = {2,4,...}, plus 0 → 1 + 200000 + 200000 = 400001 rows. Let me test that to make sure the max row count works.

Timing: 0.075s for 200000 records — excellent. Memory: well within 512 MiB (the ulimit -v 524288 didn't cause failure).

Now let me test lookup with the 1M trace, and the 400001-row image.

content.text: Build is fast (0.075s for 200k records). Let me construct a true 400001-row image and test lookups with the 1M-record trace:

arguments.command:
cd /work/tmp && python3 -c "
with open('fib_top.txt','w') as f:
    for i in range(200000):
        k = 2*i+1
        w = [(k>>48)&0xffff,(k>>32)&0xffff,(k>>16)&0xffff,k&0xffff,0,0,0,1]
        f.write(':'.join('%x'%x for x in w) + '/64 %d\n' % (i % 4294967296))
" && ( ulimit -v 524288; time /work/submit/planb64 build fib_top.txt fib_top.idx ) 2>&1 | tr '\n' ' '; echo; echo "rows=$(sed -n 2p fib_top.idx)"; head -3 fib_top.idx; tail -1 fib_top.idx
echo "=== 1M lookups against 400k-row image ==="
for m in scalar "batch 256" "batch 7" "batch 1"; do
  ( ulimit -v 524288; time /work/submit/planb64 lookup fib_top.idx trace_max.txt $m > out_top.txt ) 2>&1 | tr '\n' ' '; echo "mode=$m bytes=$(stat -c%s out_top.txt)"
done
md5sum out_top.txt; /work/submit/planb64 lookup fib_top.idx trace_max.txt batch 064 | md5sum
